info.title: Global Model Workstation Online (GMWO) API
info.description:
Try out the API using our [Interactive API Explorer](../v1/swagger).

For code examples, see our [GitHub repository](https://github.com/OxfordEconomics/gmwo-api-examples).

## Authentication

### Generating an access token

1. Visit the [API explorer page](../v1/swagger)
2. Select the *Access Token* section
3. Select the generate endpoint `/v1/access-token/generate`
    - ![API Explorer Access Token Section](./static/images/api-explorer-access-token-section.jpg)
4. Click *Try it out* on the right
5. Edit the value of the request JSON body:
    - Choose a value for the *Name* property
    - ![API Explorer Access Token Generate Try It Out](./static/images/api-explorer-access-token-generate-try-it-out.jpg)
6. Click *Execute*
7. Copy the newly-generated token from the *Value* of the JSON response body. 
> PLEASE NOTE: The token value cannot be retrieved again. The token itself contains no information and is merely a reference to metadata that is stored in a database on the API. If the original value is lost, the token should be revoked and replaced.

### Authenticating with an Access Token

For each HTTP request which requires authentication, the `Authorization` header must be set to: `Bearer {Value}`, where Value is a valid Access Token. If valid authentication is not provided, the HTTP response code is `401` and the response body *may* indicate one of the following reasons for failure:
- no authentication provided
- Access token has been revoked
- Access token is otherwise invalid

## Throttling (Request limits)

We place limits on each user's API usage to preserve system performance for our users generally, and to protect ourselves against undue cloud computing costs. There are two classes of request, detailed below, each of which has a different limit. 

For each class of request, there is a maximum number of requests that each user can make successfully in a given timespan. Once the limit is reached, subsequent requests fail with the response code `429`. The response body is of the form: `API calls quota exceeded! maximum admitted [number of requests] per [unit of time].`

Request class|Description|Endpoints|Limit
---|---|---|---
Inline requests|Requests for which the end result is generated immediately and included in the response body.|(All except those below)|50 per second
Enqueued requests|Intensive operations such as model solutions are not completed within the lifetime of the request. Instead, they are added to a queue to be executed separately. The response to such requests is a `ForecastOperation` object. One or more separate *inline* requests must be sent to await the completion of the operation. The limit applies to the rate at which operations are *queued*, regardless of the eventual duration of those operations.|`v1/operations/apply` `v1/operations/solve` `v1/operations/export`|10 per minute

For practical examples of working with enqueued operations, please see the following in our [examples](https://github.com/OxfordEconomics/gmwo-api-examples/) GitHub repository:
- [solve](https://github.com/OxfordEconomics/gmwo-api-examples/blob/main/solve/solve.ipynb)
- [export](https://github.com/OxfordEconomics/gmwo-api-examples/blob/main/export/export.ipynb)


> PLEASE NOTE: These limits, and the basis on which we apply limits, are liable to change in future

post.description: This request enqueues an operation which runs in the background. Use the /operations/{id}/await endpoint to wait for the operation to finish. It is not necessary to submit any Commands or a Commands File in order to perform a solve but, if you do, you should submit either one or the other and not both.
